text: Its a pain when something you buy often gets suddenly more expensive. The receipt feels wrong. The budget is tighter. You feel like a sucker. Its not always right, but the price increase is not always a bad thing, or not always justified. It should not be. I think, I think you can justify it if you are forced to it, for example, raw material costs, energy, transport, labor, regulation, compliance, all of that is going up. So, if you were to absorb all of that yourself, you will eventually, you will either cut corners, cut on staff, cut on maintenance, go bust. So, a price increase, a small one, may be necessary in order to preserve quality, reliability, jobs. So, in a sense, it might be better to pay a little bit more than to get a worse version of the same product. So, I think that price increases are not always bad. But it does hit people differently. If you are a very rich person, the extra dollar is nothing. If you are living on your salary, just enough to get by, it might be quite a lot. So, it does hurt. And I think if it is not communicated in a reasonable way, if the quality of the product is also going down, or executive bonuses are going up, it feels unfair. It feels like they are taking advantage of you. You have nowhere to go. And I think companies should be very careful. I mean, they do have an incentive to do that, to raise prices, especially if they know you have no alternatives. But they should explain why, they should tell you, they should give you some advance notice, they should not do the trick of shrinking the package size, saying its the same price. They can also offer loyalty discounts, or options, bulk options, cheaper options. But they should try to soften the blow. Because its not just about price, its about the relationship, its about trust. Transparency, does not guarantee that people are going to accept it, but at least its fair, and people can make up their own mind. And of course, competition is always a good check. If you have lots of competitors, you cant just raise prices to the moon, because people will go to another brand. And in a market where there is no competition, maybe the regulator needs to step in, and they should, where it is not justified. But in the end, I think price increases are fine, if they are necessary, if they are justified, if they are transparent, and if the customer gets something for it. That is the test. If they get something for it, its fine. If not, its just shifting the burden from the company to the consumer. So, I think companies do have the right to make money, they do have the right to protect their margins, but they do not have the right to say, well, we just need to. So, I think the customer should ask, why, and compare, and then decide. And if the price is going up, they should get better for it, or at least the same. Otherwise, it is a betrayal.
